codes.reward: 500 Lucky Spins · 350 Trait Rerolls · 250,000 Coins · 5,000 Gems

weapons.name: Cataclysm
weapons.note: Fast attacks with wide area effects. The consensus best pull in every tier list published so far — Zenless is the top rung and Cataclysm is the only weapon on it.

weapons.name: Cursed King
weapons.note: Reported as the strongest option below Cataclysm. One creator calls it overpowered in the current patch, which the tier lists agree with.

weapons.name: Shanks
weapons.note: Mythic sword fighter built around heavy energy slashes. Ranks at the top of the Mythic band in the tier lists checked.

weapons.name: Alucard
weapons.note: Ranged weapon with combo attacks. A healing effect is claimed by some showcases and is not confirmed by any published source — treat it as unverified.

weapons.name: Guts
weapons.note: Greatsword with heavy slams and strong single-target damage. Appears in the launch banner art and in every roster we cross-checked.

weapons.name: Lights of Divinity
weapons.note: Golden slashes and pillars of light that hit a wide area. Mythic band, area-damage role.

weapons.name: Kings Gambit
weapons.note: Area weapon that the rosters describe as a solid filler until you roll a Mythic. Good first Legendary, not an endgame pick.

weapons.name: Twisted Agony
weapons.note: Purple slashes with area damage, placed in the middle of the Legendary band. None of the sources we checked names the anime character it is based on.

weapons.name: Thunder Prodigy
weapons.note: Lightning-themed Epic weapon. An early-game option you replace when a Legendary or better drops.

weapons.name: Cosmic Warrior
weapons.note: Epic all-rounder that carries the first dungeons comfortably and stops being exciting by the mid-game.

weapons.name: Rubber Man
weapons.note: Punches with extended range. Fine for the first hours; expected to be replaced by Epic's end.

weapons.name: Hu Tao
weapons.note: Shows up in creator videos and one competitor roster, including as an evolution target. No source we checked states its rarity, so it stays unranked here.

weapons.name: Igris
weapons.note: Seen in Shadow Monarch update footage ("max upgraded OP Igris"). No published roster lists its rarity or kit yet.

weapons.name: Sung Jin-Woo
weapons.note: The chase entity of the Shadow Monarch update — creators advertise "0.01% Sung Jin-Woo" pulls. Rarity and mechanics are not documented by any published source.

systems.name: The Arsenal (Rolls and Lucky Spins)
systems.detail: Weapons are summoned here, not bought. Rolls are the common currency and Lucky Spins are the better-odds one. No official odds or pity numbers are published — any percentage you see online is community guesswork.

systems.name: Traits and rerolls
systems.detail: Traits are modifiers attached to a weapon and Trait Rerolls are the currency that changes them. Rerolls are the resource most worth hoarding — four codes alone pay out hundreds of them.

systems.name: Two weapon slots
systems.detail: You equip two weapons and swap between them mid-dungeon. Community reports two traps: some Zenless weapons refuse a second copy, and summoning while a weapon is equipped can overwrite it together with its trait. Check both slots before you roll.

systems.name: Dungeons and modes
systems.detail: The game runs a story path plus higher-intensity modes — the current update added a raid, and creators also farm an AFK chamber and Endless-style runs. Each mode has its own recommended level, which none of the reputable listings agree on yet.

systems.name: Evolution and awakening
systems.detail: Weapons evolve along a rarity ladder (Epic → Legendary → Mythic → Arcane → Zenless). Evolution generally wants a duplicate or a specific material — the exact cost per tier is unpublished.

systems.name: Accessories
systems.detail: Crafted from Gems, equipped for passive bonuses. Gems come from codes and dungeon drops, which is why gem codes disappear fast.

systems.name: Titles and quests
systems.detail: Account-level progression with their own rewards. Useful for early levelling because quest XP is free, unlike rerolls.

redeemSteps: Launch Anime Zero on Roblox and wait for your character to load in.
Open the Codes menu — it sits among the buttons on the right side of the HUD.
Paste a code exactly as written. Codes are case-sensitive, so use the copy button instead of retyping.
Press Redeem. If a code is level-gated (50KCCU-tier codes are not, but several need level 25 or 50), redeem it again once you pass the requirement.
gaps: Roll odds and pity — the game publishes neither, and every percentage circulating online is community estimate.
Trait list and exact effects — no source we checked lists the full trait table.
Accessory recipes and stat values — crafting exists, the numbers behind it are not published.
Damage formula and scaling — creator testing only, no official numbers.
The full weapon roster — rosters stop at around a dozen weapons and lag behind updates like Shadow Monarch.
"Inspired by" character mappings — community-reported, not official, and some remain unattributed.
